how: The starter proposes a shared school mark that others join by requesting border work and offering help.
The opening invites school members to make their mark, while later turns recruit concrete help.
A logo judged too big prompts a smaller version, while an organiser later invokes a lack of alternative space.
A question about popularity receives an explanation of the event as a social experiment.
Decoding must include correction during live construction because the mascot name and nearby lettering are corrected before placement ends.
The shared school mark is resized, expanded into the university name, signed with the subreddit name, and proposed for further adjustment.
Participants correct the name of the emblem being drawn while also criticizing its proposed expansion.
Members report working on the school letters and successfully adding the subreddit name.
Requests for starting location and a usable picture receive coordinates and an image anchor.
Members distribute script instructions for building and maintaining the mark and report using automation to fill it.
A participant who cannot readily use the script receives an image and coordinates that preserve a manual route into the work.
The participant closes the image clarification with thanks that ask for nothing further.
Acceptance need not be bare because an explicit offer to help also asks where the group intends to build.
Visible instructions do not establish whether organisational arrangements were decided outside the thread or test a claim about most rooms.
Participants identify damage, call for keeping the mark intact, and offer to defend both school logos.
A question about responsibility for a damaging line receives a denial and tentative attribution to throwaway accounts.
An attribution is corrected when its speaker identifies different lettering in the apparent takeover.
Scripting also serves construction and planned maintenance, so adoption cannot be explained only as a response to upkeep exceeding available hands.
Neighbouring makers contest a planned rectangle through requests to stop, announced limits, and threats to undo encroachment.
Border talk also arises from expanding the room's own lettering into existing art rather than solely from erosion of its mark.
Participants ask the group to work around existing art and reassure one maker that the announced rectangle spares their work.
An apology counts as restraint only with evidence of limiting damage because an organiser apologizes while explicitly refusing to stop overwriting.
Boundary talk need not produce restraint because one objection receives a refusal while another receives a specific assurance of safety.
Neighbours request help outlining their area and an individual later volunteers to defend both school logos without showing a reciprocal bargain.
A neighbouring group's help request and an individual's dual defence pledge do not establish a coalition between rooms.
The visitor requests help for fellow students but the passage cannot establish a mandate to act as an envoy.
Neighbouring school marks and a disputed rectangle do not show guests building under a host room's rules.
A participant explicitly links a taken-over area to new coordinates to its right.
Relocation is supported without requiring an explicit discussion weighing fighting against moving.
The relocation report names takeover but supplies no judgement that defenders were too few to hold the spot.
The refusal to stop overwriting and the neighbour's counter-threat dispute space without disputing who may bind the room.
Boundary disagreement is visible but the proposed transition to a dispute over representation is not.
An existing school identity supplies the shared university name and subreddit signature without establishing ideology or a historical quarrel.
A joke about placing over another logo supplies no history of a pre-existing quarrel.
The contested overwrite is justified by space scarcity and the joke about another logo does not name a prior tie motivating an attack.
Naming the official April Fools event and explaining it as a social experiment do not establish a prank frame imposed by the host subreddit.
A popularity question receives an explanation without establishing a host rule or boundary around canvas discussion.
The call and event explanation cannot establish a canvas-post flood or show whether host boundary intervention was needed.
The brief title presents the mark as school representation while a member reports adding the subreddit signature.
The closing reply marks the end and records the participant's account of what remained to the right.
Reporting the end and a surviving mark supplies no decision about carrying the temporary effort forward.
The closing record cannot establish whether preserving an account prompted any later continuation decision.
The lettering correction occurs during placement and the final report contains no contest over a preserved version of the event.
An organiser explicitly intends to overwrite a neighbouring work despite its maker's request to stop.
The neighbour answers the announced encroachment with a threat to undo any pixels covering their work.
Encroachment can arise through enlarging the room's own mark without an explicit call to attack a pre-existing rival.
A response framed as an apology does not establish restraint when it announces that the contested overwrite will continue.
